message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to pay the $50 jail fine or roll for doubles.

I have $217 and no get-out-of-jail cards. The other players are cash-poor with heavily mortgaged properties.

p3 is in jail with brown hotels and no monopolies. p4 has massive cash and light blue hotels worth $550-600. I will stay in jail to avoid both players' expensive properties.

Marvin Gardens blocks yellow and St Charles/States block pink. I have already failed one doubles roll, so I have two more attempts before I must pay the $50 fine.

Leaving jail would drop me to $167 and expose me to p4's light blue hotels. I will roll for doubles instead.

If I roll doubles and leave jail, I would land on Electric Company, States Avenue, Virginia Avenue, Pennsylvania Railroad, St. James Avenue, Kentucky Avenue, and then Water Works. Indiana, Illinois, and B&O are all mortgaged by p2, so they would not cost rent. Atlantic Avenue is unowned.

Boardwalk is unmortgaged but has no houses, so rent would only be $50. The dark blue threat is minimal right now because Park Place is mortgaged and Boardwalk has no hotels. The real danger remains p4's light blue hotels: Oriental and Vermont each cost $550, while Connecticut costs $600.

Mortgaging all remaining properties would yield roughly $535 in liquidity, which is more than enough to cover the $50 fine. I have already mortgaged New York Avenue, so I still have St. Charles, States, St. James, Virginia, and Water Works available to tap.

Total cash plus mortgage liquidity is roughly $752. That covers one light blue hotel, but two hits would bankrupt me. I will stay in jail and roll for doubles instead. p4 cannot complete the yellow monopoly because I own Marvin Gardens.

I own the orange monopoly but New York Avenue is mortgaged. Unmortgaging it costs $110, leaving only $107. One house on each orange would cost $300, so I cannot build anything useful right now.
